$comment: Model-name rewrites applied to vendored upstream files, in order. Each rule is a literal find/replace scoped to upstream paths by glob. `count` is the exact number of replacements the rule must make across its files; a mismatch fails the sync so upstream changes are never rewritten blindly. Team models: each member runs Claude Code (Opus 5.5, max effort). So every judgment, prose, and panel role is `inherit-parent`: it runs on the member's own agent, and panels get their independent opinions from separate runs. Code delegates are the exception the owner chose: they run on `sonnet` (Claude Sonnet 5.5), or `haiku` (Claude Haiku 5.5) for trivial mechanical edits. An explicit model name survives only as an example a user can type, and a GPT name is always `gpt-6-sol-high`.

rules.from: Families go by prefix: `claude-*`, and `grok-*` with `cursor-grok-*` and `composer-*`. A refused `composer-*` entry runs on `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast`.
Families go by prefix: `claude-*`, and `grok-*` with `cursor-grok-*` and `composer-*`. A refused `composer-*` entry runs on Reviewer B's default.
rules.to: Families go by prefix: `claude-*` and `gpt-*`. A refused `gpt-*` entry runs on Reviewer B's default.

rules.from: Map each default slug with the rows above: `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` is `opus xhigh`, and `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` is `inherit-parent`.
rules.to: Map each default slug with the rows above. A default of `inherit-parent` stays `inherit-parent`.

rules.from: So `unlimited` turns `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh` into `claude-opus-5-5-max`. Grok slugs top out at `xhigh`, so under `unlimited` the fallback puts Grok at `xhigh` and keeps `grok-4.7-xhigh-fast` as it is. `large` keeps both defaults. `small` turns them into `claude-opus-5-5-medium` and `grok-4.7-medium-fast`.

rules.from: The hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms) go to your strongest judgment model (`claude-opus-5-5-xhigh`), whether the task needs judgment on vague intent or is a precisely specified sequence of steps to execute to the letter. Trivial mechanical edits go to your fast code model.
rules.to: A feature, refactor, bug fix, perf fix, hillclimb step, or one of the hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms) goes to `sonnet` (Claude Sonnet 5.5). A trivial mechanical edit (a rename, a move, a formatting or one-line fix, or steps specified to the letter with nothing to decide) goes to `haiku` (Claude Haiku 5.5), the `trivial edits` line. The Task tool takes these aliases, not version slugs.
